## pr check-merge

Check whether a pull request can be merged

For whoever may merge (the issue’s owner, or a manager of its project). Reads the pull request from the code host now and stores what it read; `headSha` is what `merge` expects back.

```bash
nb-studio pr check-merge <issue> <pr>
```

| Argument | Description                                                   |
| -------- | ------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `issue`  | The issue the pull request is linked to (`PM-12`, or its id). |
| `pr`     | The pull request’s id in Studio (`pr list`).                  |

**Output:** One record, field by field; with `--json`, `result.data`.

**Who:** People (a sign-in or an API key).

**Request:** `POST /api/git/pullRequests/{pullRequestId}/checkMerge` (`gitCheckPullRequestMerge`)

**Examples:**

```bash
nb-studio pr check-merge PM-12 <pr>
```

## pr close

Close a pull request

For whoever may edit the issue, as for opening a pull request. Comments the reason on the pull request and closes it on the code host, as the person who asked for the work when they authorized the app, else as the repository’s connection; the issue’s activity records it with the reason. A closed pull request no longer counts for moving the issue on once the others are merged. `unlink` also unlinks it from the issue.

```bash
nb-studio pr close <issue> <pr> --reason <string>
```

| Argument | Description                                                   |
| -------- | ------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `issue`  | The issue the pull request is linked to (`PM-12`, or its id). |
| `pr`     | The pull request’s id in Studio (`pr list`).                  |

| Flag       | Type    | Description                                                                                                               |
| ---------- | ------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `--reason` | string  | Why it is closed, such as "Superseded by #15"; commented on the pull request and kept in the issue’s activity. (required) |
| `--unlink` | boolean | Also unlink it from the issue.                                                                                            |

**Output:** One record, field by field; with `--json`, `result.data`.

**Who:** People, and agents in a run; needs the action `studio.git/open-pr`.

**Request:** `POST /api/git/pullRequests/{pullRequestId}/close` (`gitClosePullRequest`)

**Examples:**

```bash
nb-studio pr close PM-12 <pr> --reason "Superseded by #15"
nb-studio pr close PM-12 <pr> --reason "No longer needed" --unlink
```

## pr edit

Edit a pull request

For whoever may edit the issue, as for opening a pull request. Changes what is given on the code host — the title, the description, the branch to merge into, draft or ready for review — as the person who asked for the work (the caller, or whoever woke the agent) when they authorized the app, else as the repository’s connection. The issue’s activity records what changed.

```bash
nb-studio pr edit <issue> <pr>
```

| Argument | Description                                                   |
| -------- | ------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `issue`  | The issue the pull request is linked to (`PM-12`, or its id). |
| `pr`     | The pull request’s id in Studio (`pr list`).                  |

| Flag      | Type    | Description                                                                                                                                                  |
| --------- | ------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `--title` | string  | The new title, such as "fix(export): keep the column order".                                                                                                 |
| `--body`  | string  | The new description, in Markdown; it replaces the old one. Write anything longer than a line to a file and pass it with --body-file. (or --body-file <path>) |
| `--base`  | string  | The branch to merge into.                                                                                                                                    |
| `--draft` | boolean | Turn it into a draft.                                                                                                                                        |
| `--ready` | boolean | Mark it ready for review.                                                                                                                                    |

**Output:** One record, field by field; with `--json`, `result.data`.

**Who:** People, and agents in a run; needs the action `studio.git/open-pr`.

**Request:** `POST /api/git/pullRequests/{pullRequestId}/edit` (`gitEditPullRequest`)

**Examples:**

```bash
nb-studio pr edit PM-12 <pr> --title "fix(export): keep the column order"
nb-studio pr edit PM-12 <pr> --body-file pr.md --ready
```

## pr link

Link a pull request to an issue

For whoever may edit the issue: a pull request opened elsewhere, which Studio then reads from the code host and follows. Once every linked pull request is merged, the issue moves on. Branches a repository’s branch rules name (`agent/<issue key>` by default) are linked automatically. Answers 201 when it was linked now, 200 when it was linked already; `meta.message` says which. An agent’s run on an issue may leave `issueId` out for its own issue.

```bash
nb-studio pr link <url>
```

| Argument | Description                                                          |
| -------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `url`    | The pull request URL, such as https://github.com/owner/repo/pull/12. |

| Flag      | Type   | Description                                                            |
| --------- | ------ | ---------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `--issue` | string | The issue, such as PM-12; in a run on an issue, that issue by default. |

**Output:** One record, field by field; with `--json`, `result.data`.

**Who:** People, and agents in a run; needs the action `studio.git/open-pr`.

**Request:** `POST /api/git/pullRequests` (`gitLinkPullRequest`)

**Examples:**

```bash
nb-studio pr link https://github.com/acme/web/pull/12 --issue PM-12
```

## pr list

List an issue’s pull requests

For whoever sees the issue. `meta` carries the suggested pull requests and what the caller may do. An agent’s run on an issue may leave `issueId` out for its own issue.

```bash
nb-studio pr list
```

| Flag      | Type   | Description                                                            |
| --------- | ------ | ---------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `--issue` | string | The issue, such as PM-12; in a run on an issue, that issue by default. |

**Output:** A list (table columns: `id`, `repo`, `number`, `state`, `ciState`, `title`); with `--json`, `result.data` is the array and `result.meta` the paging.

**Who:** People, and agents in a run; needs the action `pm.issues/view`.

**Request:** `GET /api/git/pullRequests` (`gitListPullRequests`)

**Examples:**

```bash
nb-studio pr list
nb-studio pr list --issue PM-12
```

## pr merge

Merge a pull request

For whoever may merge (the issue’s owner, or a manager of its project). Squash-merges the head `expectedHeadSha` names, as the caller when they authorized the app, else as the repository’s connection.

```bash
nb-studio pr merge <issue> <pr> --expected-head <string>
```

| Argument | Description                                                   |
| -------- | ------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `issue`  | The issue the pull request is linked to (`PM-12`, or its id). |
| `pr`     | The pull request’s id in Studio (`pr list`).                  |

| Flag              | Type    | Description                                               |
| ----------------- | ------- | --------------------------------------------------------- |
| `--expected-head` | string  | (required)                                                |
| `--yes`           | boolean | Go ahead without asking “Squash-merge this pull request?” |

**Output:** One record, field by field; with `--json`, `result.data`.

**Who:** People (a sign-in or an API key).

**Request:** `POST /api/git/pullRequests/{pullRequestId}/merge` (`gitMergePullRequest`)

**Examples:**

```bash
nb-studio pr merge PM-12 <pr> --expected-head <sha from pr check-merge>
```

## pr open

Open a pull request for an issue

For whoever may edit the issue; push the branch first. Opens the pull request on the code host and links it to the issue at once: on the repository of the issue’s project (its first linked one unless `repo` names another), from the run’s branch (the repository’s first branch rule, `agent/PM-12` by default) unless `head` names another, as the person who asked for the work (the caller, or whoever woke the agent) when they authorized the app, else as the repository’s connection. Once every linked pull request is merged, the issue moves on. An agent’s run on an issue may leave `issueId` out for its own issue.

```bash
nb-studio pr open --title <string>
```

| Flag      | Type    | Description                                                                                                                                                                                |
| --------- | ------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `--issue` | string  | The issue, such as PM-12; in a run on an issue, that issue by default.                                                                                                                     |
| `--title` | string  | The title, following the repository’s commit convention, such as "fix(export): keep column order". Studio links the pull request to the issue, so the title needs no issue key. (required) |
| `--body`  | string  | The description, in Markdown. Write anything longer than a line to a file and pass it with --body-file. (or --body-file <path>)                                                            |
| `--repo`  | string  | The repository, as owner/name, when the project has several.                                                                                                                               |
| `--head`  | string  | The branch with the change; your run’s branch by default.                                                                                                                                  |
| `--base`  | string  | The branch to merge into; the working directory’s default branch by default.                                                                                                               |
| `--draft` | boolean | Open it as a draft.                                                                                                                                                                        |

**Output:** One record, field by field; with `--json`, `result.data`.

**Who:** People, and agents in a run; needs the action `studio.git/open-pr`.

**Request:** `POST /api/git/pullRequests/open` (`gitOpenPullRequest`)

**Examples:**

```bash
nb-studio pr open --title "fix(export): keep column order" --body-file pr.md
nb-studio pr open --issue PM-12 --title "fix(export): keep column order" --head fix/export --draft
```

## pr reopen

For whoever may edit the issue, as for opening a pull request. Reopens a closed (not merged) pull request on the code host, as the person who asked for the work when they authorized the app, else as the repository’s connection; the issue’s activity records it.

```bash
nb-studio pr reopen <issue> <pr>
```

| Argument | Description                                                   |
| -------- | ------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `issue`  | The issue the pull request is linked to (`PM-12`, or its id). |
| `pr`     | The pull request’s id in Studio (`pr list`).                  |

**Output:** One record, field by field; with `--json`, `result.data`.

**Who:** People, and agents in a run; needs the action `studio.git/open-pr`.

**Request:** `POST /api/git/pullRequests/{pullRequestId}/reopen` (`gitReopenPullRequest`)

**Examples:**

```bash
nb-studio pr reopen PM-12 <pr>
```

## pr update

Update an issue’s pull request link

For whoever may edit the issue. `autoCompleteDisabled` says whether the pull request counts for moving the issue on when merged.

```bash
nb-studio pr update <issue> <pr> --auto-complete-disabled
```

| Argument | Description                                                   |
| -------- | ------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `issue`  | The issue the pull request is linked to (`PM-12`, or its id). |
| `pr`     | The pull request’s id in Studio (`pr list`).                  |

| Flag                       | Type    | Description |
| -------------------------- | ------- | ----------- |
| `--auto-complete-disabled` | boolean | (required)  |

**Output:** One record, field by field; with `--json`, `result.data`.

**Who:** People (a sign-in or an API key); needs the action `pm.issues/edit`.

**Request:** `PATCH /api/git/pullRequests/{pullRequestId}` (`gitUpdatePullRequest`)
